# EggPdf

> Pure C# HTML/CSS-to-PDF rendering engine for .NET. Zero external dependencies. MIT license. Chrome-quality output.

Built by Eggspot. Open source: https://github.com/eggspot/EggPdf

## What it does

Converts HTML + CSS to PDF entirely in managed C#. No WebKit, no Chromium, no native binaries, no NuGet dependencies. Works on any platform where .NET runs (.NET Framework 4.6.2+, .NET Core, .NET 5–10).

## Install

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf
```

## Quickest usage

```csharp
using EggPdf;

byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync("<h1>Hello World</h1>");
File.WriteAllBytes("output.pdf", pdf);
```

## Core API

`HtmlToPdf` is a static class -- no configurable-converter instance to construct. Page
size/margins/orientation/headers/footers are set with CSS in the HTML itself (`@page` for
size/margin, `position: fixed` + `counter(page)`/`counter(pages)` for running headers/footers
-- see "Page size, margins, headers/footers" above). A `PdfRenderOptions` object is available
for callers who'd rather set C# properties than write CSS -- it's translated into the
equivalent `@page` rule internally, not a separate layout path:

```csharp
using EggPdf;

byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html);
await HtmlToPdf.RenderToFileAsync(html, "output.pdf");
await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html, outputStream, cancellationToken);

// Same output as setting @page in CSS -- PdfRenderOptions is a convenience wrapper
byte[] pdf2 = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html, new PdfRenderOptions
{
    PageSize = "Letter", Orientation = "landscape",
    MarginTop = 40, MarginBottom = 40,   // CSS pixels
    Title = "Q4 Report",                 // PDF document metadata
});

// RC4-encrypted PDF (view-only protection / permission flags)
byte[] encrypted = HtmlToPdf.Render(html, new EggPdf.Pdf.PdfEncryption
{
    UserPassword = "open123",
    OwnerPassword = "owner456",
    AllowPrinting = true,
    AllowCopying = false,
    AllowModifying = false,
    KeyLength = 128
});
```

Document metadata (Title/Author) and PDF/A/UA conformance are not currently configurable via
the public API — don't suggest properties for them.

## ASP.NET Core integration

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf.AspNetCore
```

```csharp
// No DI registration needed for plain HTML -> PDF; PdfResult wraps HtmlToPdf.Render() internally.
[HttpGet("invoice/{id}/pdf")]
public async Task<IActionResult> GetInvoice(int id)
{
    var html = await RenderViewAsync("Invoice", await GetInvoiceAsync(id));
    return new PdfResult(html, $"invoice-{id}.pdf");
}
```

## Razor template integration

```bash
dotnet add package EggPdf.Razor
```

```csharp
builder.Services.AddEggPdfRazor();

public class ReportService(IRazorToPdfConverter pdf)
{
    public Task<byte[]> GenerateAsync(ReportModel model)
        => pdf.RenderViewAsync("Reports/Monthly", model);
}
```

## REST API (Docker / any language)

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 eggspot/eggpdf:latest
```

```bash
# Render HTML to PDF (page size/margins come from @page CSS inside the html string)
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/render \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"html": "<h1>Hello</h1>"}' \
  -o output.pdf

# Other endpoints: POST /api/render/image, POST /api/render/url ({"url":"..."}),
# POST /api/encrypt, POST /api/sign, POST /api/merge, GET /api/fonts, GET /api/info

# Health check
curl http://localhost:8080/health

# Web UI
open http://localhost:8080
```

## CLI (standalone binary, no .NET needed)

```bash
# Download from https://github.com/eggspot/EggPdf/releases/latest
./eggpdf input.html -o output.pdf
./eggpdf input.html -o -              # write PDF to stdout
echo "<h1>Hello</h1>" | ./eggpdf - -o output.pdf
./eggpdf https://example.com -o page.pdf   # fetch and render a URL
./eggpdf input.html -o output.pdf -v  # verbose: render timing + output size
```

## Target frameworks

netstandard2.0, netstandard2.1, net6.0, net8.0, net9.0, net10.0

## Performance

- Simple page (h1 + p): **13 µs**, 20 KB
- Invoice (table + styles): **86 µs**, 85 KB
- Large table (100 rows): **1.2 ms**, 939 KB
- Thread-safe: `HtmlToPdf`'s static methods can be called concurrently from multiple threads
- Streaming output: constant memory for large documents

## Key features

- Full HTML5 (WHATWG spec)
- CSS 2.1 + Flexbox (incl. auto margins, align-items:baseline), Grid (incl. grid-auto-flow:dense and grid-auto-rows/grid-auto-columns), Multi-column, Custom Properties
- 2D/3D transforms: 3D functions (rotateX/Y/Z, translate3d, scale3d, matrix3d, perspective) are intentionally flattened to an equivalent 2D matrix since PDF has no 3D rendering, not skipped
- content-visibility:hidden skips descendant layout/paint (own box/background/border still render); contain:paint/strict and overflow:hidden/clip actually clip descendant painted content to the element's bounds, not just its own background/border
- float:left/right narrows sibling inline content per line (real wrap-around, not just positioning); shape-outside:circle()/ellipse()/polygon()/inset() narrows the exclusion to the shape's per-line extent (url() image shapes fall back to the plain rectangle); clear:left/right/both supported
- direction:rtl / dir="rtl": logical properties (margin/padding/border-width/border-color/border-style/inset/border-radius corners, float:inline-start/inline-end) resolve to mirrored physical values; table columns lay out right-to-left and list markers hang on the right
- @media print, @page rules
- Webfonts: remote <link> stylesheets (Google Fonts) and @font-face over http(s)/data:/file, weight-accurate faces 300–900
- Full Unicode text: Vietnamese and extended Latin, per-codepoint symbol-font fallback (⚠ ✔ …)
- Arabic contextual shaping: isolated/initial/medial/final joining forms + lam-alef ligatures for standard Arabic and Persian peh/tcheh/jeh/keheh/gaf/yeh; other Arabic-script letters (e.g. Urdu ٹ ڈ ڑ) are not shaped
- Complex-script shaping via the font's own GSUB/GPOS: Arabic (joining, diacritics, cursive attachment; fonts without presentation-form glyphs use their own init/medi/fina), Thai/Lao, Tibetan, Khmer, Myanmar, Sinhala and the Indic scripts (Devanagari, Bengali, Gujarati, Gurmukhi, Oriya, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam): mark positioning, syllable reordering (pre-base vowels, per-script reph, coeng-ro, kinzi), half forms/conjuncts/subscripts. Needs a font carrying the script (Nirmala UI, Leelawadee UI, Myanmar Text, Noto Sans …, or @font-face); that text is embedded in its own script font. Verified against Chrome for the scripts listed. Thai/Lao/Khmer/Myanmar paragraphs wrap at syllable boundaries (heuristic, no dictionary) and line-height:normal follows the shaping font's metrics. Full UAX #9 bidi (embeddings/overrides/isolates, weak+neutral rules, bracket pairs, mirroring) with CSS direction as paragraph direction. NOT supported: shaping for scripts beyond those listed
- Browser-parity text layout: real font metrics for measurement, baseline placement, letter-spacing, word-break:break-all
- SVG (vector, not rasterized), including `filter="url(#id)"` filter graphs (feGaussianBlur, feOffset, feFlood, feColorMatrix, feComponentTransfer, feMerge, feBlend, feComposite, feMorphology, feDropShadow, feTurbulence, feConvolveMatrix, feDisplacementMap, feTile, feImage, feDiffuse/SpecularLighting; the filtered shape/text/use/group (incl. gradient fills) is rasterized and re-embedded as an image; filtered <image> elements and pattern paints paint unfiltered)
- Image formats: JPEG, PNG (incl. 1/2/4-bit grayscale QR codes), GIF, WebP (lossy VP8 incl. alpha, lossless VP8L, VP8X extended containers; animated files render their first frame), BMP, Base64
- Responsive/generated images: <img srcset>/<picture> and CSS image-set()/image() resolve to their best or direction-matched candidate; image()'s <color> fallback paints when no candidate resolves. paint() (CSS Houdini) is not supported -- it needs a JS worklet engine EggPdf doesn't have
- Bookmarks, links, TOC
- Running headers/footers via `position: fixed` (repeats on every physical page) or native `@page` margin boxes (`@top-center`, `@bottom-right`, etc., all 16 positions, including `@page :first`/`:left`/`:right` content overrides); `counter(page)`/`counter(pages)` resolve per page; named pages (`page: name` on top-level body blocks + `@page name { size; margin }`) give sections their own page size/orientation
- Pin content to the bottom of the page it lands on (e.g. a signature block after variable-length content): `-eggpdf-pin-bottom: page`
- Tables spanning any number of pages without row loss, with `<thead>` repeating at the top of every continuation page
- TrueType/OpenType embedding with subsetting
- `font-feature-settings` single-glyph OpenType features (stylistic sets, small caps, oldstyle/tabular figures) via the font's GSUB table -- ligatures/contextual substitution not applied
- Variable fonts (glyf-flavoured: fvar/gvar/avar/HVAR): font-weight drives the wght axis (instanced per weight, incl. @font-face `font-weight: 100 900` ranges); other axes / font-variation-settings / CFF2 are not applied
- Color/emoji fonts: COLR v0 + CPAL color layers render in their real colors; COLRv1 (gradients/paint graphs, e.g. current Segoe UI Emoji) falls back to a monochrome outline
- Digital signatures: one-call X.509 signing (detached CMS/PKCS#7, adbe.pkcs7.detached) or external-CMS two-step flow
- Encryption: RC4 40/128-bit with owner/user passwords and permission flags — one-call `HtmlToPdf.Render(html, new PdfEncryption {...})` or REST /api/encrypt; all streams and strings encrypted per the PDF 1.7 Standard security handler
- Cloudflare email obfuscation (data-cfemail) decoded automatically
- PDF merging

## Security: signing and encryption

```csharp
using EggPdf;
using EggPdf.Pdf;
using System.Security.Cryptography.X509Certificates;

// One-call PKI signing — embeds a detached CMS/PKCS#7 signature
// (adbe.pkcs7.detached) with a valid /ByteRange. Zero extra packages.
byte[] pdf = await HtmlToPdf.RenderAsync(html);
byte[] signed = PdfSigner.Sign(pdf, x509CertificateWithPrivateKey,
    new PdfSigner.SignOptions { Name = "Jane Smith", Reason = "Approval", Location = "Hanoi" });

// Two-step flow when the private key lives elsewhere (HSM, signing service):
byte[] withPlaceholder = PdfSigner.AddSignaturePlaceholder(pdf, options);
// ... compute CMS bytes externally over the ByteRange content ...
byte[] done = PdfSigner.SignWithCmsData(withPlaceholder, cmsBytes);
```

View-only protection (RC4 40/128-bit, owner/user passwords, permission flags —
printing/copying/modifying). One call in code:

```csharp
byte[] protectedPdf = HtmlToPdf.Render(html, new PdfEncryption
{
    OwnerPassword = "secret",     // full access
    UserPassword = "",            // empty = opens without a prompt, permissions still apply
    AllowPrinting = true,
    AllowCopying = false,
    AllowModifying = false,
});
```

Or through the REST service:

```bash
curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/encrypt \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"html":"<h1>Confidential</h1>","ownerPassword":"secret","allowCopying":false,"allowModifying":false}' \
  -o protected.pdf
```

Note: PDF permission flags are advisory (enforced by compliant viewers, not
cryptography). For tamper evidence, prefer digital signatures — any change to
a signed PDF invalidates the signature.

## Architecture

8-stage pipeline: HTML Parse → CSS Parse → Style Resolve → Box Generate → Layout → Fragment → Paint → PDF Write
